functions: followLine (b4), called in a forever loop by b3
control_flow: The start block loops forever and calls followLine again and again.
followLine: if the line tracker reads less than 30 % (black), curve left; else if it reads more than 70 % (white band or pale floor), curve right; else drive straight at 20 %.

likely_intent.description: Follow the black line through its curves all the way to the green goal at the line's end, without leaving the line.

decision_points.condition: first: the line tracker reads less than 30 %; second: it reads more than 70 %

branches.outcome: not black, more than 70 % (white band or pale floor): it curves right

branches.reason: The middle reading happens only briefly at the edge of the black core, while the robot crosses it.
branches.outcome: between 30 % and 70 %: it drives straight at 20 %

input_dimensions.dimension: where the robot starts relative to the line

scenarios.coded_response: It curves left on black, curves right on the white band or pale floor, and drives straight only in the moment it crosses the black line's edge.
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot starts on a line that runs straight and then bends, with nothing in its way; or it starts beside the line, on the side the program curves towards.
scenarios.trigger: The line tracker sees black, then the white band or pale floor, again and again while the robot moves.
scenarios.title: Follows the line through the curves to the green goal
assumptions: The green goal is a goal area at the end of the line.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It follows the line through its curves to the green goal at the line's end and stays on the line on the way.

uncertainties: The middle reading (30 % to 70 %) exists only for a moment at the edge of the black core, so the straight drive is taken only while the robot crosses the line's edge.
You didn't say where the green goal is: the tests take it as an area at the end of the line.
A start beside the line only works on the side the program curves towards (its right): on the other side it curves away and never finds the line.
The program reads no obstacle sensor, so it cannot see walls or boxes and would bump into them; nothing about obstacles is tested.
